Branch network reached 2,236 with 183 new branches opened in FY26
Funding sanctions of ₹2,897 Cr in hand plus ₹7,212 Cr in pipeline

timeline.summary: CreditAccess India B.V., via CEO Koen J. Slobbe, declared no encumbrance on CreditAccess Grameen Limited shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) for FY2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,597.27 Cr (+13.6% YoY), net profit ₹339.55 Cr (+619.2% YoY).

Q4 & FY26 investor presentation (8 May 2026): FY26 PAT ₹778 Cr (+46.3%), AUM ₹29,590 Cr (+14.0%) after ₹1,968 Cr of write-offs; FY27 guidance set at 20-25% AUM growth, 12.8-13.2% NIM and 3.0-4.0% credit cost.
CreditAccess Grameen reported Q4FY26 PAT of ₹339.5 Cr (+619.4% YoY) and AUM of ₹29,590 Cr (+14.0% YoY), guiding FY27 AUM growth at 20-25%.
Deepti Ramani, CFO, shared Q4 FY26 results conference call recording on May 8, 2026, available at the company’s website.
Q4 & FY26 earnings call (8 May 2026): FY26 credit cost 6.74% versus 5.5-6.0% guidance; FY27 guided at 20-25% AUM growth, 12.8-13.2% NIM, 3.0-4.0% credit cost and 16-20% ROE.
CreditAccess Grameen received a ₹0.03 Cr RBI penalty on May 29, 2026, for software lapses in transaction monitoring.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,903.74 Cr (+26.2% YoY), net profit ₹501.57 Cr (+298.7% YoY).
CreditAccess Grameen reported Q2FY27 results with a 299% YoY rise in PAT to ₹502 Cr, driven by asset quality normalisation and strong liability management.
2026-10-22: CreditAccess Grameen raised FY27 ROA guidance to 5.2-5.8% and ROE to 21-24% after Q2FY27 PAT of ₹501.6 Cr (+298.7% YoY) and a 50 bps loan price cut from October.
Deepti Ramani, Company Secretary, shared Q2 FY27 results conference call recording on October 22, 2026, via company website.
CreditAccess Grameen raised its FY27 ROA guidance to 5.2-5.8% following a record quarterly PAT of ₹502 Cr in Q2FY27.

watchlist.response: Band widened to absorb evolving externalities from global issues; April trends held at Q4 levels, and the view on lower versus upper end will come as the year progresses.
watchlist.text: Why the FY27 credit cost band is as wide as 3.0-4.0% and how much is higher ECL provisioning

watchlist.response: Lower credit cost will be partly passed to customers through pricing; borrowing cost has bottomed and hedging costs have risen.
watchlist.text: NIM guidance midpoint of 13% is well below the 14.2% Q4 exit

watchlist.response: Inflationary buffer built in for global issues; if they do not prolong, cost-to-income may not rise.
watchlist.text: Cost-to-income guidance of 33-35% implies costs growing faster than income

watchlist.response: Regulatory ceiling has moved from 15% to 25% to 40%; mix can be managed via securitisation, portfolio sale or co-lending.
watchlist.text: How the 60-40 MFI mix will be maintained under a 20-25% ten-year CAGR

status_history.evidence: Gross Stage 3 at 1.79% as of September 30, 2026, down from 3.17% at March 2026.

watchlist.response: Management said a 50 bps MFI price cut may come in Q3 FY27 and another 50 bps in Q4, linked to credit cost, and that repricing takes 15-18 months.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked why FY27 ROE guidance is retained despite a 24.4% Q1 ROE and what pricing cut would follow.

watchlist.response: Management said the range was kept for the West Asia crisis and monsoon, and it may end towards the lower end if no upside risks appear.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on whether the 3-4% credit cost guidance embeds cushion versus the 2.8-2.9% annualised Q1 run rate.

watchlist.response: Management said branch and people expansion is already budgeted and a ₹41 Cr West Asia overlay is in place; further overlay possible if weather plays out in Q2.

status_history.evidence: Drought-related challenges observed in 6 districts of Maharashtra in October.

watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether higher ROA should be used for overlays or branch and employee expansion.
Shareholders to approve Sharp & Tannan as joint statutory auditor from FY28

status_history.evidence: Q2FY27 credit cost ₹299 Cr, down 43.2% YoY; FY27 guidance retained at 3.0-4.0%.

watchlist.response: NIMs are at historical highs and the cut is guided by a pricing policy that factors in credit costs. If borrowing costs rise significantly, the company can reprice or skip the next planned cut.
watchlist.text: Why cut lending rates when cost of borrowing is likely to increase?

watchlist.response: Momentum is expected to accelerate in H2. The current low growth is due to high write-offs of 3 lakh customers in the past 12 months and graduation to retail products.
watchlist.text: Borrower growth appears to be in single digits/undershooting.
